Registry tests use block types defined here, which shows that\nthe loop never names a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks\nfrom mdparser.blocks import (\n    DOCUMENT,\n    PARAGRAPH,\n    Block,\n    BlockRegistry,\n    BlockType,\n    Cursor,\n    DocumentParser,\n    indent_columns,\n    next_column,\n    parse_lines,\n)\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_contents(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.content for child in block.children if child.kind is PARAGRAPH]\n\n\n# --- Column helpers ---\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_space_advances_one() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\" \", 3) == 4\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_tab_advances_to_next_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 0) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 2) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 4) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_spaces() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"   x\", 0, 0) == 3\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_expands_a_leading_tab_to_four() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_pads_a_tab_after_spaces_to_the_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"  \\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_two_tabs_as_eight() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\t\\tx\", 0, 0) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_is_zero_without_leading_whitespace() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"x  \", 0, 0) == 0\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_starts_from_the_given_column() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 2) == 2\n\n\n# --- Cursor ---\n\n\ndef test_cursor_rest_starts_as_the_whole_line() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"abc\").rest == \"abc\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_blank_for_empty_and_whitespace_lines() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\").is_blank()\n    assert Cursor(\" \\t \").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_not_blank_with_text() -> None:\n    assert not Cursor(\"  a\").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_nonspace_tracks_column_across_a_tab() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"  \\t x\")\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    assert cursor.pos == 4\n    assert cursor.col == 5\n    assert cursor.rest == \"x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_columns_consumes_whole_tab_when_it_overshoots() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"\\tx\")\n    cursor.advance_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.pos == 1\n    assert cursor.col == 4\n    assert cursor.rest == \"x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_columns_stops_at_the_target_column() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"    x\")\n    cursor.advance_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"  x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_indent_reports_columns_to_next_text() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\\t\\tx\").indent == 8\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_to_moves_by_characters() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"abc\")\n    cursor.advance_to(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"c\"\n\n\n# --- Empty and blank input ---\n\n\ndef test_empty_input_gives_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_one_empty_line_gives_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([\"\"]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_blank_lines_only_give_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([\"\", \"  \", \"\\t\", \" \\t \"]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_leading_and_trailing_blank_lines_add_no_blocks() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"\", \" \", \"word\", \"\", \"\\t\", \"\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\n# --- Paragraphs ---\n\n\ndef test_single_line_makes_one_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"hello\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"hello\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_separates_paragraphs() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"\", \"two\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"one\", \"two\"]\n\n\ndef test_repeated_blank_lines_separate_paragraphs_without_extra_blocks() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"\", \"\", \"\", \"two\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_consecutive_lines_stay_in_one_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"first\", \"second\", \"third\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"first\\nsecond\\nthird\"]\n\n\ndef test_continuation_lines_drop_their_leading_indentation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"first\", \"      second\", \"\\tthird\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"first\\nsecond\\nthird\"]\n\n\ndef test_first_line_drops_leading_spaces() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"  word\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\ndef test_final_spaces_and_tabs_are_removed_from_content() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"word \\t  \"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\ndef test_trailing_spaces_on_an_interior_line_are_kept() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"foo  \", \"bar\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"foo  \\nbar\"]\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_is_closed_when_document_ends() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"word\"])\n    assert all(not child.is_open for child in root.children)\n    assert not root.is_open\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_is_closed_by_a_blank_line_before_the_next_one() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"\", \"two\"])\n    assert [child.is_open for child in root.children] == [False, False]\n\n\ndef test_document_root_is_a_container_with_no_content() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"a\"])\n    assert root.kind is DOCUMENT\n    assert root.content == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_raw_lines_are_recorded_as_read() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"   two\"])\n    assert root.children[0].lines == [\"one\", \"two\"]\n\n\ndef _shape(root: Block) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(child.kind.name, child.content) for child in root.children]\n\n\ndef test_parsing_the_same_lines_twice_gives_the_same_tree() -> None:\n    lines = [\"a\", \"\", \"b\", \"c\"]\n    assert _shape(parse_lines(lines)) == _shape(parse_lines(lines))\n\n\n# --- Registry ---\n\n\ndef test_registry_rejects_a_duplicate_block_type_name() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        registry.register(PARAGRAPH)\n\n\ndef test_default_registry_start_rules_are_the_thematic_break_atx_heading_and_indented_code() -> None:\n    assert blocks.DEFAULT_REGISTRY.starts() == (\n        blocks.THEMATIC_BREAK,\n        blocks.ATX_HEADING,\n        blocks.INDENTED_CODE,\n    )\n\n\ndef test_lazy_block_type_must_accept_lines() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        BlockType(\"bad\", continues=lambda block, cursor: True, lazy=True)\n\n\ndef test_leaf_block_type_must_have_an_add_line_rule() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        BlockType(\"bad\", continues=lambda block, cursor: True, accepts_lines=True)\n\n\n# --- Extensibility: block types registered without changing the loop ---\n\n\ndef _rule_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.strip(\" \\t\") == \"***\":\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RULE)\n    return None\n\n\nRULE = BlockType(\"rule\", continues=lambda block, cursor: False, start=_rule_start)\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_interrupts_a_paragraph() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"a\", \"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\", \"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"a\", \"b\"]\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_closes_an_unmatched_block_before_it_starts() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert root.children[0].is_open is False\n\n\ndef _raw_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.startswith(\"<<\"):\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RAW)\n    return None\n\n\nRAW = BlockType(\n    \"raw\",\n    continues=lambda block, cursor: True,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    add_line=lambda block, cursor: block.lines.append(cursor.rest),\n    start=_raw_start,\n)\n\n\ndef test_start_rule_is_not_tried_inside_a_non_interruptible_leaf() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RAW)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"<<\", \"***\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"raw\"]\n    assert root.children[0].lines[-1] == \"***\"\n\n\n# --- Lazy paragraph continuation, via a test-only container ---\n\n\ndef _quote_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    index = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if cursor.line[index : index + 1] == \">\":\n        cursor.advance_to(index + 1)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _quote_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    index = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if cursor.line[index : index + 1] == \">\":\n        cursor.advance_to(index + 1)\n        return Block(QUOTE)\n    return None\n\n\nQUOTE = BlockType(\"quote\", continues=_quote_continues, is_container=True, start=_quote_start)\n\n\ndef quote_registry() -> BlockRegistry:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(QUOTE)\n    return registry\n\n\ndef test_quote_holds_its_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", \"> b\"], quote_registry())\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"quote\"]\n    assert kinds(root.children[0]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root.children[0]) == [\"a\\nb\"]\n\n\ndef test_unmarked_line_is_a_lazy_continuation_of_the_quote_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", \"b\"], quote_registry())\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root.children[0]) == [\"a\\nb\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_ends_the_lazy_continuation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", [\"b\"]\n\n\ndef test_document_parser_can_be_driven_one_line_at_a_time() -> None:\n    parser = DocumentParser(quote_registry())\n    parser.incorporate_line(\"> a\")\n    assert {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EUjnpJn5bHrXNXbkmTuSku","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f455b850-6ce2-4a1e-8751-d1dabca4fa32","uuid":"3504066c-e636-4faf-9951-401d04e8704a","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:26:00.143Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py","oldString":"    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")","newString":"    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'","originalFile":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":73,"oldLines":3,"newStart":73,"newLines":12,"lines":["     if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":","         return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"","     raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")","+","+","+def _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:","+    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"","+    assert block.fence is not None","+    language = block.fence.language","+    if not language:","+        return \"<code>\"","+    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01EUjnpJn5bHrXNXbkmTuSku","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Otherwise an unclosed fenced code block would\n    gain a blank line.\n    \"\"\"\n    if lines and lines[-1] == \"\":\n        lines = lines[:-1]\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)","originalFile":"\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\"\"\"\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, lambda raw: inlines.parse_inline(raw, root.references))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0.\"\"\"\n    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()\n    try:\n        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))\n        html = render_lines(lines)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        html = \"\"\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":26,"oldLines":7,"newStart":26,"newLines":14,"lines":[" "," "," def render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:","-    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\"\"\"","+    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.","+","+    A final line ending terminates the last line rather than starting an empty one, so the one empty","+    entry that `split_lines` leaves after it is dropped. source = \"```\" + language + \" extra words\\ncode\\n```\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert ('class=\"language-' + language + '\"') in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_closing_fence_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence of the other character, or a shorter fence, does not close the block.\"\"\"\n    other = \"~~~\"\n    shorter = \"```\"\n    source = \"````\\naaa\\n\" + other + \"\\n\" + shorter + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert other in result.stdout\n    assert shorter in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_unclosed_runs_to_end(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed fence consumes the rest of the document as code.\"\"\"\n    trailing = \"still code\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"```\\nfirst\\n\\n\" + trailing + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n    assert trailing in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence interrupts a paragraph and text after The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\nThe corpus section examples that use quotes, lists and setext headings are gated in the lists story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Fence, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef fenced_blocks(lines: list[str]):\n    \"\"\"The top-level fenced code blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is FENCED_CODE]\n\n\ndef code_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level fenced code block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in fenced_blocks(lines)]\n\n\ndef fence_of(lines: list[str]) -> Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of the only top-level fenced code block that `lines` produce.\"\"\"\n    (block,) = fenced_blocks(lines)\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    return block.fence\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_fenced_backtick_and_tilde(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Backtick and tilde fences each render one pre element containing the supplied body.\"\"\"\n    body = \"some body text\"\n    for fence in (\"```\", \"~~~\"):\n        source = fence + \"\\n\" + body + \"\\n\" + fence + \"\\n\"\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n        assert body in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_info_string_language_class(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string becomes the language class.\"\"\"\n    language = \"ruby\"\n    source = \"```\" + language + \" extra words\\ncode\\n```\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\nThe corpus section examples that use quotes, lists and setext headings are gated in the lists story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Fence, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef fenced_blocks(lines: list[str]):\n    \"\"\"The top-level fenced code blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is FENCED_CODE]\n\n\ndef code_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level fenced code block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in fenced_blocks(lines)]\n\n\ndef fence_of(lines: list[str]) -> Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of the only top-level fenced code block that `lines` produce.\"\"\"\n    (block,) = fenced_blocks(lines)\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    return block.fence\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_fenced_backtick_and_tilde(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Backtick and tilde fences each render one pre element containing the supplied body.\"\"\"\n    body = \"some body text\"\n    for fence in (\"```\", \"~~~\"):\n        source = fence + \"\\n\" + body + \"\\n\" + fence + \"\\n\"\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n        assert body in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_info_string_language_class(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string becomes the language class.\"\"\"\n    language = \"ruby\"\n    source = \"```\" + language + \" extra words\\ncode\\n```\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert ('class=\"language-' + language + '\"') in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_closing_fence_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence of the other character, or a shorter fence, does not close the block.\"\"\"\n    other = \"~~~\"\n    shorter = \"```\"\n    source = \"````\\naaa\\n\" + other + \"\\n\" + shorter + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert other in result.stdout\n    assert shorter in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_unclosed_runs_to_end(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed fence consumes the rest of the document as code.\"\"\"\n    trailing = \"still code\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"```\\nfirst\\n\\n\" + trailing + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n    assert trailing in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence interrupts a paragraph and text after it starts a new paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"foo\\n```\\nbar\\n```\\nbaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_fenced_two_backticks_not_a_fence(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Two backticks do not open a fence; they form a code span instead.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"``\\nfoo\\n``\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<code>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_fenced_indentation_stripped(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Content indentation up to the fence indentation is removed, and unindented lines are kept.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \" ```\\n aaa\\naaa\\n```\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == gated in the lists story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Fence, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef fenced_blocks(lines: list[str]):\n    \"\"\"The top-level fenced code blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is FENCED_CODE]\n\n\ndef code_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level fenced code block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in fenced_blocks(lines)]\n\n\ndef fence_of(lines: list[str]) -> Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of the only top-level fenced code block that `lines` produce.\"\"\"\n    (block,) = fenced_blocks(lines)\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    return block.fence\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_fenced_backtick_and_tilde(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Backtick and tilde fences each render one pre element containing the supplied body.\"\"\"\n    body = \"some body text\"\n    for fence in (\"```\", \"~~~\"):\n        source = fence + \"\\n\" + body + \"\\n\" + fence + \"\\n\"\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n        assert body in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_info_string_language_class(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string becomes the language class.\"\"\"\n    language = \"ruby\"\n    source = \"```\" + language + \" extra words\\ncode\\n```\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert ('class=\"language-' + language + '\"') in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_closing_fence_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence of the other character, or a shorter fence, does not close the block.\"\"\"\n    other = \"~~~\"\n    shorter = \"```\"\n    source = \"````\\naaa\\n\" + other + \"\\n\" + shorter + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert other in result.stdout\n    assert shorter in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_unclosed_runs_to_end(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed fence consumes the rest of the document as code.\"\"\"\n    trailing = \"still code\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"```\\nfirst\\n\\n\" + trailing + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n    assert trailing in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence interrupts a paragraph and text after it starts a new paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"foo\\n```\\nbar\\n```\\nbaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_fenced_two_backticks_not_a_fence(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Two backticks do not open a fence; they form a code span instead.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"``\\nfoo\\n``\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<code>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_fenced_indentation_stripped(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Content indentation up to the fence indentation is removed, and unindented lines are kept.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \" ```\\n aaa\\naaa\\n```\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"aaa\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\" aaa\") == 0\n\n\n# --- Block tree: opening fence assert kinds([fence, \"code\", fence]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"indent\", [0, 1, 2, 3])\ndef test_fence_indented_up_to_three_columns_starts_a_block(indent: int) -> None:\n test_backtick_info_string_with_a_backtick_is_not_a_fence() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"``` aa ```\", \"foo\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_tilde_info_string_may_contain_a_backtick() -> None:\n The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\nThe corpus section examples that use quotes, lists and setext headings are gated in the lists story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Fence, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef fenced_blocks(lines: list[str]):\n    \"\"\"The top-level fenced code blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is FENCED_CODE]\n\n\ndef code_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level fenced code block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in fenced_blocks(lines)]\n\n\ndef fence_of(lines: list[str]) -> Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of the only top-level fenced code block that `lines` produce.\"\"\"\n    (block,) = fenced_blocks(lines)\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    return block.fence\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_fenced_backtick_and_tilde(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Backtick and tilde fences each render one pre element containing the supplied body.\"\"\"\n    body = \"some body text\"\n    for fence in (\"```\", \"~~~\"):\n        source = fence + \"\\n\" + body + \"\\n\" + fence + \"\\n\"\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n        assert body in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_info_string_language_class(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string becomes the language class.\"\"\"\n    language = \"ruby\"\n    source = \"```\" + language + \" extra words\\ncode\\n```\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert ('class=\"language-' + language + '\"') in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_closing_fence_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence of the other character, or a shorter fence, does not close the block.\"\"\"\n    other = \"~~~\"\n    shorter = \"```\"\n    source = \"````\\naaa\\n\" + other + \"\\n\" + shorter + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert other in result.stdout\n    assert shorter in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_unclosed_runs_to_end(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed fence consumes the rest of the document as code.\"\"\"\n    trailing = \"still code\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"```\\nfirst\\n\\n\" + trailing + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n    assert trailing in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence interrupts a paragraph and text after it starts a new paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"foo\\n```\\nbar\\n```\\nbaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_fenced_two_backticks_not_a_fence(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Two backticks do not open a fence; they form a code span instead.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"``\\nfoo\\n``\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<code>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_fenced_indentation_stripped(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Content indentation up to the fence indentation is removed, and unindented lines are kept.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \" ```\\n aaa\\naaa\\n```\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"aaa\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\" aaa\") == 0\n\n\n# --- Block tree: opening fence ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"fence\", [\"```\", \"~~~\", \"````\", \"~~~~~\"])\ndef test_fence_of_three_or_more_characters_starts_a_block(fence: str) -> None:\n    assert kinds([fence, \"code\", fence]) == [FENCED_CODE.name]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"fence\", [\"``\", \"~~\", \"`\", \"~\"])\ndef test_fewer_than_three_characters_do_not_start_a_block(fence: str) -> None:\n    assert kinds([fence, \"code\", fence]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"indent\", [0, 1, 2, 3])\ndef test_fence_indented_up_to_three_columns_starts_a_block(indent: int) -> None:\n    assert kinds([\" \" * indent + \"```\", \"code\", \"```\"]) == [FENCED_CODE.name]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"indent\", [4, 5, 8])\ndef test_fence_indented_four_or_more_columns_is_not_a_fence(indent: int) -> None:\n    assert kinds([\" \" * indent + \"```\", \"code\"]) == [INDENTED_CODE.name]\n\n\ndef test_backtick_info_string_with_a_backtick_is_not_a_fence() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"``` aa ```\", \"foo\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_tilde_info_string_may_contain_a_backtick() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"~~~ aa ```\", \"foo\", \"~~~\"]) == [FENCED_CODE.name]\n\n\ndef test_fence_interrupts_a_paragraph() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"foo\", \"```\", \"bar\", \"```\"]) == is FENCED_CODE\n    assert paragraph.kind is PARAGRAPH\n\n\ndef test_two_fenced_blocks_in_a_row_are_separate() -> None:\n    assert code_contents([\"```\", \"a\", \"```\", \"```\", \"b\", \"```\"]) == \"~~~\"]).language == \"js\"\n\n\ndef test_backslash_escape_in_info_string_is_removed() -> None:\n    assert fence_of([\"```foo\\\\+bar\", \"x\", \"```\"]).language == \"foo+bar\"\n\n\ndef test_entity_in_info_string_is_decoded() -> None:\n    assert fence_of([\"```&ouml;kl\", \"x\", \"```\"]).language == \"ökl\"\n\n\ndef test_opening_fence_records_its_character_and_length() -> None:\n    fence = fence_of([\"~~~~ rust\", \"x\", \"~~~~\"])\n    assert (fence.char, fence.length) == (\"~\", 4)\n\n\ndef test_opening_fence_records_its_indentation() -> None:\n    assert fence_of([\"  ```\", \"x\", \"```\"]).indent == 2\n\n\n# --- Block tree: content ---\n\n\ndef test_content_lines_are_joined_with_line_endings() -> None:\n    assert code_contents([\"```\", \"a\", \"b\", \"```\"]) == code_contents([\"```\", \"a\", \"\", \"b\", \"```\"]) == [\"a\\n\\nb\\n\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"indent\", [0, 1, 2, 3])\ndef test_content_loses_up_to_the_opening_indentation(indent: int) ->  assert code_contents([\"   ```\", \"aaa\", \"```\"]) == [\"aaa\\n\"]\n\n\ndef test_content_indentation_beyond_the_fence_is_kept() -> None:\n    assert code_contents([\"```\", \"    indented\", (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f455b850-6ce2-4a1e-8751-d1dabca4fa32","uuid":"b4a3e5c2-c36b-444e-9ac8-da3bbc8e5e10","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:27:09.585Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_fenced_code.py","oldString":"from mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Fence, parse_lines","newString":"from mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Block, Fence, parse_lines","originalFile":"\"\"\"Fenced code block tests: the seven declared checks from FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md, then block-tree and\nexact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\nThe corpus section examples that use quotes, lists and setext headings are gated in the lists story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Fence, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef fenced_blocks(lines: list[str]):\n    \"\"\"The top-level fenced code blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is FENCED_CODE]\n\n\ndef code_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n gated in the lists story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Block, input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is FENCED_CODE]\n\n\ndef code_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level fenced code block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in fenced_blocks(lines)]\n\n\ndef fence_of(lines: list[str]) -> Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of the only top-level fenced code block that `lines` produce.\"\"\"\n    (block,) = fenced_blocks(lines)\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    return block.fence\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_fenced_backtick_and_tilde(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Backtick and tilde fences each render one pre element source = \"```\" + language + \" extra words\\ncode\\n```\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert ('class=\"language-' + language + '\"') in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_closing_fence_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence of the other character, or a shorter fence, does not print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert other in result.stdout\n    assert shorter in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_unclosed_runs_to_end(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed fence consumes the rest of the document as code.\"\"\"\n    trailing = \"still code\"\n    result = The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\nThe corpus section examples that use quotes, lists and setext headings are gated in the lists story\nand are not run here.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import FENCED_CODE, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, Block, Fence, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef fenced_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[Block]:\n    \"\"\"The top-level fenced code blocks that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child for child in parse_lines(lines).children if child.kind is FENCED_CODE]\n\n\ndef code_contents(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The content of each top-level fenced code block, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [block.content for block in fenced_blocks(lines)]\n\n\ndef fence_of(lines: list[str]) -> Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of the only top-level fenced code block that `lines` produce.\"\"\"\n    (block,) = fenced_blocks(lines)\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    return block.fence\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_fenced_backtick_and_tilde(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Backtick and tilde fences each render one pre element containing the supplied body.\"\"\"\n    body = \"some body text\"\n    for fence in (\"```\", \"~~~\"):\n        source = fence + \"\\n\" + body + \"\\n\" + fence + \"\\n\"\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n        assert body in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_info_string_language_class(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string becomes the language class.\"\"\"\n    language = \"ruby\"\n    source = \"```\" + language + \" extra words\\ncode\\n```\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert ('class=\"language-' + language + '\"') in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_closing_fence_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence of the other character, or a shorter fence, does not close the block.\"\"\"\n    other = \"~~~\"\n    shorter = \"```\"\n    source = \"````\\naaa\\n\" + other + \"\\n\" + shorter + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert other in result.stdout\n    assert shorter in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_unclosed_runs_to_end(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed fence consumes the rest of the document as code.\"\"\"\n    trailing = \"still code\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"```\\nfirst\\n\\n\" + trailing + \"\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n    assert trailing in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence interrupts a paragraph and text after it starts a new paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"foo\\n```\\nbar\\n```\\nbaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_fenced_two_backticks_not_a_fence(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Two backticks do not open a fence; they form a code span instead.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"``\\nfoo\\n``\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<code>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_fenced_indentation_stripped(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Content indentation up to the fence indentation is removed, and unindented lines are kept.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \" ```\\n aaa\\naaa\\n```\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"aaa\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\" aaa\") == 0\n\n\n# --- Block tree: opening fence ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"fence\", [\"```\", \"~~~\", \"````\", \"~~~~~\"])\ndef test_fence_of_three_or_more_characters_starts_a_block(fence: str) -> None:\n    assert kinds([fence, \"code\", fence]) == [FENCED_CODE.name]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"fence\", [\"``\", \"~~\", \"`\", \"~\"])\ndef test_fewer_than_three_characters_do_not_start_a_block(fence: str) -> None:\n    assert kinds([fence, \"code\", fence]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"indent\", [0, 1, 2, 3])\ndef test_fence_indented_up_to_three_columns_starts_a_block(indent: int) -> None:\n \"\"\"The opening fence of the only top-level fenced code block that `lines` produce.\"\"\"\n    (block,) = fenced_blocks(lines)\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    return block.fence\n\n\n# --- source = \"```\" + language + \" extra words\\ncode\\n```\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert ('class=\"language-' + language + '\"') in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_closing_fence_rules(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A fence of the other character, or a shorter fence, does not print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n    assert other in result.stdout\n    assert shorter in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_fenced_unclosed_runs_to_end(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unclosed fence consumes the rest of the document as code.\"\"\"\n    trailing = \"still code\"\n    result =
